code_label: Quantum computing framed as advantageous for optimization
text_span: Quantum computers are composed of quantum bits, or qubits, which can be in a state of superposition.
rationale: Defines the quantum property motivating the paper's approach to computational problems.

code_label: Quantum advantage for simultaneous evaluation
text_span: Quantum computers continue to highlight their efficacy through their ability to evaluate potential solutions simultaneously
rationale: States the claimed advantage of quantum computing relevant to optimization and simulation.

code_label: Finance as a target application area
text_span: which is particularly useful in finance.
rationale: Identifies finance as the application domain motivating the study.

code_label: Software foundation for future finance applications
text_span: our goal is to contribute to the software foundation for the future of quantum applications in finance.
rationale: Explicitly states the study's broader contribution beyond the simple case.

code_label: Use of IBM Quantum System One at RPI
text_span: we utilized IBM’s Quantum System One, a state-of-the-art quantum computer housed at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.
rationale: Specifies the physical quantum hardware used in the study.

code_label: Prioritized access reduced queue times
text_span: we have full and prioritized access to this on-campus quantum computer, which significantly reduces job queue wait times
rationale: Describes an operational advantage affecting experimentation workflow.

code_label: 127-qubit Eagle processor
text_span: The quantum computer employed in this study features 127 qubits, powered by an IBM Quantum ’Eagle’ Processor
rationale: Provides a key hardware specification relevant to the implementation.

code_label: Testing on simulator before hardware execution
text_span: Before sending out jobs to the physical quantum computer, we conducted extensive testing on IBM’s quantum simulator.
rationale: Describes the development workflow used before running on hardware.

code_label: Portfolio uses three asset classes
text_span: the portfolio consisted of three asset classes, US equities, international equities, and global fixed income.
rationale: Defines the asset universe used in the simulation.

code_label: Historical indices used as proxies
text_span: We used the past 20 years’ historical data of S&P 500, MSCI All Country World Index ex US, and Bloomberg Global Aggregate indices as the proxy
rationale: Specifies the data sources used to estimate inputs.

code_label: Volatility and covariance estimated from history
text_span: to calculate the volatilities and covariance matrix.
rationale: States the statistical quantities derived from historical data.

code_label: Expected returns set exogenously
text_span: The expected returns are chosen to be 10%, 10%, and 6% respectively for the three asset classes.
rationale: Reports the return assumptions used in the model.

code_label: Monthly multivariate log-normal simulation
text_span: The simulations assume multivariate log-normal distribution and are done monthly.
rationale: Describes the distributional assumption and time granularity.

code_label: Classical benchmark uses multivariate normal distribution
text_span: The classical method for performance simulation involves calculating the multivariate normal distribution.
rationale: States the classical comparison method.

code_label: Quantum circuit generates discretized normal distribution
text_span: the quantum computer executes a specialized quantum circuit that produces a normal distribution discretized over a specified number of qubits.
rationale: Describes the quantum modeling approach used to generate returns.

code_label: Three qubits per asset class
text_span: we allocate 3 qubits to each of the three asset classes, resulting in a qubit array of [3, 3, 3].
rationale: Specifies the discretization choice for each asset class.

code_label: More qubits can improve accuracy
text_span: For more complex scenarios or when higher accuracy is required, additional qubits can be utilized.
rationale: Indicates a scalability path for improved fidelity.

code_label: Bounds set to three standard deviations
text_span: The distribution bounds are set to three standard deviations above and below the expected returns.
rationale: Specifies the truncation range used in the distribution construction.

code_label: Circuit built from qubit array, mean, covariance, and bounds
text_span: With the qubit array, expected return µ, the covariance matrix Σ, and bounds defined, the quantum circuit for the multivariate normal distribution is generated.
rationale: Summarizes the inputs required to generate the quantum circuit.

code_label: Circuit construction uses qubits and gates
text_span: The circuit is then constructed by applying a sequence of quantum gates—analogous to classical logic gates—which manipulate the qubits’ states
rationale: Describes the gate-based implementation of the algorithm.

code_label: Combined circuit measured for execution
text_span: These two quantum circuits are then combined. After measuring this combined circuit, a quantum circuit ready for execution is obtained.
rationale: Explains how the final executable circuit is formed.

code_label: Each execution simulates 10 years
text_span: Each execution runs 120 shots of the quantum circuit, with each shot representing the returns for one month. Therefore, each execution simulates 10 years of performance.
rationale: Defines the mapping from shots to simulated horizon.

code_label: Output covariance checked against input
text_span: we convert the qubit measurements into returns and compare the covariance matrix of the input with that of the output to ensure that the quantum computer’s inherent errors are minimal.
rationale: States the validation check used to assess fidelity.

code_label: Sample covariance difference reported
text_span: A sample of the difference is provided below.
rationale: Introduces the reported discrepancy between input and output covariance.

code_label: Rebalancing rules tested
text_span: With the generated return data, we implemented different types of rebalancing rules including monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, and annually.
rationale: Describes the portfolio management rules applied to the simulated returns.

code_label: More qubits should improve accuracy
text_span: theoretically, using more qubits would enhance simulation accuracy
rationale: States a theoretical expectation about increasing qubit count.

code_label: Circuit build time is the main limitation
text_span: The main limitation of this method lies in the time required to build the quantum circuit.
rationale: Explicitly identifies the principal bottleneck.

code_label: Three-qubit-per-asset circuit builds quickly on emulator
text_span: On the quantum emulator, running a qubit array of [3, 3, 3] allows the circuit to be built within a few seconds.
rationale: Reports emulator performance for the smallest tested configuration.

code_label: Larger circuits take longer to construct on emulator
text_span: increasing the array to [4, 4, 4] results in a circuit that takes approximately one minute to construct.
rationale: Reports the scaling of build time with circuit size.

code_label: Largest emulator test took about 20 minutes
text_span: The most extensive test we performed used a qubit array of [5, 5, 5], which required about 20 minutes to build.
rationale: Reports the upper-end emulator build time observed.

code_label: Hardware run succeeded for smallest circuit
text_span: When running the circuit on a physical quantum computer, the [3, 3, 3] qubit array completed in just a few seconds.
rationale: Reports successful execution on physical hardware for the smallest case.

code_label: Hardware build time increased for medium circuit
text_span: With the [4, 4, 4] qubit array, the build time increased to 30 seconds
rationale: Reports hardware performance for the medium configuration.

code_label: Largest hardware test failed
text_span: with the [5, 5, 5] qubit array, the quantum computer failed after around 6 minutes.
rationale: Reports a failure on the physical quantum computer for the largest configuration.

code_label: Emulator and hardware can diverge
text_span: Functional circuits that work well on an emulator often exhibit significant discrepancies when run on a physical quantum computer.
rationale: States a caveat about simulator-to-hardware transfer.

code_label: Quantum computers are becoming accessible
text_span: they have become reasonably accessible, enabling students to conduct research in various fields, including finance in our case.
rationale: Observes increased accessibility and its research implications.

code_label: Need for software development to keep pace
text_span: As quantum hardware development accelerates in the coming decade, software development will need to keep pace.
rationale: Identifies a forward-looking need for software progress.

code_label: Student quantum community seen as crucial
text_span: We believe that the availability of quantum computers to college students is crucial for establishing a quantum software community.
rationale: Expresses a normative claim about community-building.

code_label: Quantum supremacy framed as a future goal
text_span: help bring quantum supremacy closer to reality.
rationale: States a broader aspirational outcome of the work and ecosystem.
